newsitem.title: FRANCE: SocGen to join reshuffle of media shares - paper.
newsitem.headline: SocGen to join reshuffle of media shares - paper.

text.p: French bank Societe Generale plans to swap its stake in Canal Plus for a larger share in media group Havas, echoing a similar plan reportedly being considered by Generale des Eaux, daily Le Figaro reported on Tuesday.
A Societe Generale spokesman declined to comment.
Generale des Eaux and Havas said in a joint statement on Monday they were in talks on their respective audiovisual media interests, primarily in pay-tv station Canal Plus.

Press reports say the plan is for Generale des Eaux to transfer its 19.2 percent stake in Canal Plus to Havas, nearly doubling Havas's existing 21.6 percent shareholding in Canal Plus. Havas would then increase its own capital through a reserved issue to allow Generale des Eaux a bigger stake.
Le Figaro said Societe Generale, which owns 4.5 percent of Canal Plus, would carry out an identical exercise.
"(Generale des Eaux) and Societe Generale will convey their shareholdings in Canal Plus to Havas," it said.
The newspaper gave no source for the article.
Havas shares soared on Monday and those of Generale jumped too after news of the joint media talks, which analysts described as positive for all parties involved.
